newsitem.title: GERMANY: German post staff step up protests against new law.
newsitem.headline: German post staff step up protests against new law.

text.p: German post workers on Friday warned further industrial action was planned over the weekend after some 16,000 staff took part in protests against a new law aimed at removing the German post office's monopoly.

The action comes as speculation mounts that the German postal market will be freed up to competition earlier and more completely than previously expected because of pressure from some politicians within the Bonn coalition.
The Deutsche Postgewerkschaft (DPG) union said workers at some 80 sorting centres across Germany had participated in work stoppages beginning with the late shift on Thursday.
DPG, which had earlier said it was not aiming at widespread disruption of the postal service, said there had nonetheless been some impact on letter distribution.
Rallies also took place outside regional offices of the Christian Democrat and Free Democrat (FDP) Bonn coalition partners, the DPG said.
It added that further stoppages were planned at sorting centres later on Friday and Saturday and that a demonstration involving some 10,000 people was planned for Monday in Bonn.

Government sources have said that opposition from FDP politicians will likely mean that earlier plans by post minister Wolfgang Boetsch to grant the post office a five-year exclusive operator licence will not be approved.

Moreover, the part of the market reserved for the existing post office is now thought likely to be limited to letters up to 100 grammes in weight, and not the 350 grammes that Boetsch had initially envisaged.

The DPG fears that the new postal law, due to be agreed next week, will open the market up to "cherry-picking", in which rival operators will from the end of this year be able to operate in the most lucrative parts of the market, ignoring the least attractive market segments.
It said such a move could put tens of thousands of existing post office jobs at risk.
DPG and opposition politicians want a postal law that would guarantee a high degree of universal service and allow the Post AG post office sufficient scope to finance its general postal services.

"The government coalition of post robbers is endangering both a universal postal service and the security of the jobs involved," said Hans Martin Bury, parliamentary spokesman on the postal sector for the opposition SPD party.
